hook: The police are holding my brother and **won't let him go.**
hook_q: How long can police keep someone before a Magistrate?

slides.title: The limit is **24 hours.**
slides.body: Police can't keep a person arrested without a warrant in custody longer than is reasonable, and never beyond 24 hours without a Magistrate's special order.

slides.title: Travel time **isn't counted.**
slides.body: The 24 hours don't include the time needed for the journey from the place of arrest to the Magistrate's court.

slides.title: No **unnecessary delay.**
slides.body: Police must take or send the arrested person, without unnecessary delay, before a Magistrate having jurisdiction, or the officer in charge of a police station.

slides.title: Need more time? **Go to a Magistrate.**
slides.body: Probe can't finish in 24 hours, and there are grounds to believe the accusation is well-founded? The officer in charge or investigating officer (sub-inspector or above) must send a copy of the diary entries to the nearest Magistrate and forward the accused.

slides.title: First remand: up to **15 days.**
slides.body: The Magistrate can authorise custody for up to 15 days, in whole or in parts, within the first 40 days (60 days for offences punishable with death, life or 10+ years). Longer needs adequate grounds.

timeline.text: Maximum detention if the offence is punishable with **death, life** or 10 years or more.
If the probe isn't finished, the accused shall be released on bail if ready to furnish it.

sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 57, 58 (NCRB, ncrb.mha.gov.in)
BNSS 2023 – Section 187, as reproduced in Delhi High Court, Neeraj Kumar v. State NCT of Delhi, Bail Appln. 190/2026 (delhihighcourt.nic.in)
caption:
How long can the police keep you before a Magistrate? 👇

1️⃣ Without a Magistrate's special order, no more than 24 hours
2️⃣ Travel time from the place of arrest to the court isn't counted
3️⃣ Police must take you before a Magistrate without unnecessary delay
4️⃣ The Magistrate can first order custody for up to 15 days (in whole or in parts); longer detention needs adequate grounds
5️⃣ Total detention during investigation: 90 days if the offence is punishable with death, life or 10+ years, 60 days for others. After that, bail if you're ready to furnish it

Source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 57, 58, 187
